content: Do not act as if you had ten thousand years to throw away. Death stands at your elbow. Be good for something while you live and it is in your power.
author: Marcus Aurelius
story:
Written in military campaign tents along the freezing Danube River during the Marcomannic Wars (170–180 CE), Marcus wrestled with the Antonine Plague, the betrayal of General Avidius Cassius, and the crushing responsibilities of the Roman Empire. In his private journal, he strictly commanded himself to master his judgments, embrace cosmic duty, and remain uncorrupted by imperial power.

In formulating this reflection, Marcus Aurelius stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of urgency. For Marcus Aurelius, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
reflectionPrompt: What would change in your daily outlook if you truly lived by this perspective?
